findings.where: Motion sketch section, the full-width lavender panel at the foot of the page (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The whole motion section sits on a large lavender ground. That colour is in none of the tile's four named colours, and the house has no purple. It is the loudest area on the page, and it breaks the direction's rule of paper, grey ink and blue on the wordmark and links only. Inside it, the blue link and the blue curve sit on a third hue.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for the house blue and grey as the only ink on one soft ground. Mark, whose purple stage backdrop the palette notes say was deliberately turned to grey. A purple slab makes the sheet look built from leftover colours rather than the house's.

findings.where: Pad yellow: the palette swatch says 'the address strip', but the first screen and the rest of the page have no yellow panel
findings.fault: The direction's one colour memory of the legal pad is used nowhere on the page a visitor sees. The palette gives it the job of the address strip, but no address strip is rendered. Yellow appears only as a sliver inside the texture sample, so the colour is listed but has no use.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who said the legal pad is 'saveable with careful intention' and judges the first screen first. Without the yellow, v1 reads as plain ivory and grey and loses the one thing that makes it Counsel's paper and not a generic off-white tile.

findings.where: Palette row, the four swatches (desktop-02, phone-01)
findings.fault: The four colour chips are four different shapes and edges: a square-cornered box with a grey hairline, a rounded rectangle, an ellipse, and a square box with a thick blue border. Like samples are not treated alike. The yellow chip's blue outline also looks like a selected or focused state, not a colour sample.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the palette as the tile's statement of restraint. The mixed shapes look careless, and the ellipse and blue-edged box suggest rounded corners and blue borders that the paper's square hairline frame rules out.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lectern photograph (desktop-03 to -04, phone-02 to -03)
findings.fault: The greyscale photo is a large slab of near-#404040 dark grey across the full text column. It is the heaviest dark area on the sheet. The palette note says photographs are multiplied onto the paper and take its warmth, but the render shows a flat, cold, dark block on the ivory page.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and readers of Mark's articles. Every article photo with a coloured backdrop would come out as a heavy dark rectangle breaking the quiet paper, the opposite of the 'journal' look the note promises.

findings.where: Texture sample, the bordered box with a yellow bar along its bottom edge (desktop-02 to -03, phone-02)
findings.fault: The pad-yellow fill stops about 60% of the way across the box's bottom edge. It looks like a half-loaded progress bar or a rendering slip, not a sample of the yellow strip.
findings.who_objects: The founder, inspecting the texture specimen. A part-filled bar looks unfinished and says nothing clear about how the yellow strip would sit.
